scope: Whole synchronization function lines 254-416 and path grouping helpers 61-116 reviewed. Original synchronize_files and original rfigc.main executed unchanged using temporary authored files.

findings.detail: On failed post-repair database verification, r_row[-3] is written unconditionally, but r_row exists only when report_file is truthy. With valid database and no report file, three identically incorrect copies yield a written incorrect output and then UnboundLocalError. Reproduced end to end.
Without a database, synchronization does not provide independent content verification. Majority tie false success from v7 remains possible; database check is optional, not an unconditional safeguard.

Pre-check can select a currently valid source and then copyfile reopens it without reusing a verified stable handle. Post-check covers output against database when correctly handled, but source selection is not an atomic snapshot.

If voting reports ambiguity but final output passes database, code marks hash OK and appends an explanatory message, yet retains errcode nonzero. Consumers must distinguish recovered-valid content from clean voting.
Output paths are written directly and validated afterward, without staging/atomic publish or rollback on failed verification. Failed outputs remain in target directory.

first_direct_control_exit_zero_meaning: The harness successfully reproduced and asserted the original failure; not a claim that upstream synchronization succeeded.
